¶ Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and threescore and six talents of gold;
Beside that which chapmen and merchants brought. And all the kings of Arabia and governors of the country brought gold and silver to Solomon.
¶ And king Solomon made two hundred targets of beaten gold: six hundred shekels of beaten gold went to one target.
And three hundred shields made he of beaten gold: three hundred shekels of gold went to one shield. And the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.
Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with pure gold.
And there were six steps to the throne, with a footstool of gold, which were fastened to the throne, and stays on each side of the sitting place, and two lions standing by the stays:
And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps. There was not the like made in any kingdom.

¶ And all the drinking vessels of king Solomon were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold: none were of silver; it was not any thing accounted of in the days of Solomon.
For the king’s ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Huram: every three years once came the ships of Tarshish bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.
And King Solomon passed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
¶ And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, that ELOHIYM had put in his heart.
And they brought every man his present, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and raiment, harness, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year.
¶ And Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen; whom he bestowed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Yerushalayim.
¶ And he reigned over all the kings from the river even unto the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt.
And the king made silver in Yerushalayim as stones, and cedar trees made he as the sycomore trees that are in the low plains in abundance.
And they brought unto Solomon horses out of Egypt, and out of all lands.

¶ Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, are they not written in The Book of Nathan the Prophet, and in the Prophecy of AhiYah the Shilonite, and in The Visions of Iddo the Seer against Yarob’am the son of Nebat?
And Solomon reigned in Yerushalayim over all YisraEL forty years.
And Solomon slept with his fathers, and he was buried in the city of David his father: and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.
And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for to Shechem were all YisraEL come to make him king.
And it came to pass, when Yarob’am the son of Nebat, who was in Egypt, whither he had fled from the presence of Solomon the king, heard it, that Yarob’am returned out of Egypt.
And they sent and called him. So Yarob’am and all YisraEL came and spake to Rehoboam, saying,
Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore ease thou somewhat the grievous servitude of thy father, and his heavy yoke that he put upon us, and we will serve thee.
And he said unto them, Come again unto me after three days. And the people departed.
¶ And king Rehoboam took counsel with the old men that had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, What counsel give ye me to return answer to this people?
And they spake unto him, saying, If thou be kind to this people, and please them, and speak good words to them, they will be thy servants for ever.
But he forsook the counsel which the old men gave him, and took counsel with the young men that were brought up with him, that stood before him.
And he said unto them, What advice give ye that we may return answer to this people, which have spoken to me, saying, Ease somewhat the yoke that thy father did put upon us?

And the young men that were brought up with him spake unto him, saying, Thus shalt thou answer the people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it somewhat lighter for us; thus shalt thou say unto them, My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.
For whereas my father put a heavy yoke upon you, I will put more to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
So Yarob’am and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king bade, saying, Come again to me on the third day.
And the king answered them roughly; and King Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men,
And answered them after the advice of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add thereto: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
So the king hearkened not unto the people: for the cause was of ELOHIYM, that the YAHAWAH might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of AhiYah the Shilonite to Yarob’am the son of Nebat.

¶ And when all YisraEL saw that the king would not hearken unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? and we have none inheritance in the son of Yishai: every man to your tents, O YisraEL: and now, David, see to thine own house. So all YisraEL went to their tents.
But as for the children of YisraEL that dwelt in the cities of Yehuda, Rehoboam reigned over them.

Then king Rehoboam sent Hadoram that was over the tribute; and the children of YisraEL stoned him with stones, that he died. But king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Yerushalayim.
And YisraEL rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

And when Rehoboam was come to Yerushalayim, he gathered of the house of Yehuda and Benyamin an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men, which were warriors, to fight against YisraEL, that he might bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam.
But the word of the YAHAWAH came to ShemaYah the man of ELOHIYM, saying,
Speak unto Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Yehuda, and to all YisraEL in Yehuda and Benyamin, saying,

Thus saith the YAHAWAH, Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren: return every man to his house: for this thing is done of me. And they obeyed the words of the YAHAWAH, and returned from going against Yarob’am.
¶ And Rehoboam dwelt in Yerushalayim, and built cities for defence in Yehuda.
He built even Beth-lehem, and Etam, and Tekoa,
And Beth-zur, and Shoco, and Adullam,
And Gath, and Mareshah, and Ziph,
And Adoraim, and Lachish, and Azekah,
And Zorah, and Aiyalon, and Hebron, which are in Yehuda and in Benyamin fenced cities.
And he fortified the strong holds, and put captains in them, and store of victual, and of oil and wine.
And in every several city he put shields and spears, and made them exceeding strong, having Yehuda and Benyamin on his side.
¶ And the priests and the Levites that were in all YisraEL resorted to him out of all their coasts.
For the Levites left their suburbs and their possession, and came to Yehuda and Yerushalayim: for Yarob’am and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest’s office unto the YAHAWAH:
And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.
And after them out of all the tribes of YisraEL such as set their hearts to seek the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of YisraEL came to Yerushalayim, to sacrifice unto the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of their fathers.
So they strengthened the kingdom of Yehuda, and made Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong, three years: for three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon.
¶ And Rehoboam took him Mahalath the daughter of Yerimoth the son of David to wife, and Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Yishai;
Which bare him children; Ye’us, and ShamarYah, and Zaham.
And after her he took Maachah the daughter of Absalom; which bare him AbiYah, and Attai, and Ziza, and Shelomith.

And Rehoboam loved Maachah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines: (for he took eighteen wives, and threescore concubines; and begat twenty and eight sons, and threescore daughters.)
And Rehoboam made AbiYah the son of Maachah the chief, to be ruler among his brethren: for he thought to make him king.
And he dealt wisely, and dispersed of all his children throughout all the countries of Yehuda and Benyamin, unto every fenced city: and he gave them victual in abundance. And he desired many wives.
And it came to pass, when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the YAHAWAH, and all YisraEL with him.
And it came to pass, that in the fifth year of King Rehoboam Shishak king of Egypt came up against Yerushalayim, because they had transgressed against the YAHAWAH,
With twelve hundred chariots, and threescore thousand horsemen: and the people were without number that came with him out of Egypt; the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians.
And he took the fenced cities which pertained to Yehuda, and came to Yerushalayim.

¶ Then came ShemaYah the prophet to Rehoboam, and to the princes of Yehuda, that were gathered together to Yerushalayim because of Shishak, and said unto them, Thus saith the YAHAWAH, Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak.
Whereupon the princes of YisraEL and the king humbled themselves; and they said, The YAHAWAH TSIDQENU.

And when the YAHAWAH saw that they humbled themselves, the word of the YAHAWAH came to ShemaYah, saying, They have humbled themselves; therefore I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance; and my wrath shall not be poured out upon Yerushalayim by the hand of Shishak.
Nevertheless they shall be his servants; that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.

So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Yerushalayim, and took away the YAHAWAH treasures of the house of the YAHAWAH, and the treasures of the king’s house; he took all: he carried away also the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
Instead of which king Rehoboam made shields of brass, and committed them to the hands of the chief of the guard, that kept the entrance of the king’s house.
And when the king entered into the house of the YAHAWAH, the guard came and fetched them, and brought them again into the guard chamber.
And when he humbled himself, the wrath of the YAHAWAH turned from him, that he would not destroy him altogether: and also in Yehuda things went well.

¶ So King Rehoboam strengthened himself in Yerushalayim, and reigned: for Rehoboam was one and forty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Yerushalayim, the city which the YAHAWAH had chosen out of all the tribes of YisraEL, to put his name there. And his mother’s name was Naamah an Ammonitess.
And he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek the YAHAWAH.

Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, are they not written in The Book of ShemaYah the Prophet, and of Iddo the Seer concerning genealogies? And there were wars between Rehoboam and Yarob’am continually.
And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David: and AbiYah his son reigned in his stead.
Now in the eighteenth year of king Yarob’am began AbiYah to reign over Yehuda.
He reigned three years in Yerushalayim. His mother’s name also was MichaYah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between AbiYah and Yarob’am.

And AbiYah set the battle in array with an army of valiant men of war, even four hundred thousand chosen men: Yarob’am also set the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, being mighty men of valour.
¶ And AbiYah stood up upon mount Zemaraim, which is in mount Ephraim, and said, Hear me, thou Yarob’am, and all YisraEL;
Ought ye not to know that the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of YisraEL gave the kingdom over YisraEL to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
Yet Yarob’am the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, is risen up, and hath rebelled against his master.

And there are gathered unto him vain men, the children of Belial, and have strengthened themselves against Rehoboam the son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and tenderhearted, and could not withstand them.
And now ye think to withstand the kingdom of the YAHAWAH in the hand of the sons of David; and ye be a great multitude, and there are with you golden calves, which Yarob’am made you for elohiyms.

Have ye not cast out the priests of the YAHAWAH, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made you priests after the manner of the nations of other lands? so that whosoever cometh to consecrate himself with a young bullock and seven rams, the same may be a priest of them that are no elohiyms.
But as for us, the YAHAWAH is our ELOHIYM, and we have not forsaken him; and the priests, which minister unto the YAHAWAH, are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites wait upon their business:

And they burn unto the YAHAWAH every morning and every evening burnt sacrifices and sweet incense: the shewbread also set they in order upon the pure table; and the candlestick of gold with the lamps thereof, to burn every evening: for we keep the charge of the YAHAWAH our ELOHIYM; but ye have forsaken him.

And, behold, ELOHIYM himself is with us for our captain, and his priests with sounding trumpets to cry alarm against you. O children of YisraEL, fight ye not against the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of your fathers; for ye shall not prosper.
¶ But Yarob’am caused an ambushment to come about behind them: so they were before Yehuda, and the ambushment was behind them.
And when Yehuda looked back, behold, the battle was before and behind: and they cried unto the YAHAWAH, and the priests sounded with the trumpets.
Then the men of Yehuda gave a shout: and as the men of Yehuda shouted, it came to pass, that ELOHIYM smote Yarob’am and all YisraEL before AbiYah and Yehuda.
And the children of YisraEL fled before Yehuda: and ELOHIYM delivered them into their hand.
And AbiYah and his people slew them with a great slaughter: so there fell down slain of YisraEL five hundred thousand chosen men.
Thus the children of YisraEL were brought under at that time, and the children of Yehuda prevailed, because they relied upon the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of their fathers.
And AbiYah pursued after Yarob’am, and took cities from him, Beth-el with the towns thereof, and Yeshanah with the towns thereof, and Ephrain with the towns thereof.
Neither did Yarob’am recover strength again in the days of AbiYah: and the YAHAWAH struck him, and he died.
¶ But AbiYah waxed mighty, and married fourteen wives, and begat twenty and two sons, and sixteen daughters.
And the rest of the acts of AbiYah, and his ways, and his sayings, are written in the story of the prophet Iddo.
So AbiYah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa his son reigned in his stead. In his days the land was quiet ten years.
And Asa did that which was good and right in the eyes of the YAHAWAH his ELOHIYM:
For he took away the altars of the strange elohiyms, and the high places, and brake down the images, and cut down the groves:
And commanded Yehuda to seek the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment.
Also he took away out of all the cities of Yehuda the high places and the images: and the kingdom was quiet before him.
And he built fenced cities in Yehuda: for the land had rest, and he had no war in those years; because the YAHAWAH had given him rest.

Therefore he said unto Yehuda, Let us build these cities, and make about them walls, and towers, gates, and bars, while the land is yet before us; because we have sought the YAHAWAH our ELOHIYM, we have sought him, and he hath given us rest on every side. So they built and prospered.

And Asa had an army of men that bare targets and spears, out of Yehuda three hundred thousand; and out of Benyamin, that bare shields and drew bows, two hundred and fourscore thousand: all these were mighty men of valour.
¶ And there came out against them Zerah the Ethiopian with an host of a thousand thousand, and three hundred chariots; and came unto Mareshah.
Then Asa went out against him, and they set the battle in array in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

And Asa cried unto the YAHAWAH his ELOHIYM, and said, YAHAWAH, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O YAHAWAH our ELOHIYM; for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude. O YAHAWAH, thou art our ELOHIYM; let not man prevail against thee.
So the YAHAWAH smote the Ethiopians before Asa, and before Yehuda; and the Ethiopians fled.

And Asa and the people that were with him pursued them unto Gerar: and the Ethiopians were overthrown, that they could not recover themselves; for they were destroyed before the YAHAWAH, and before his host; and they carried away very much spoil.
And they smote all the cities round about Gerar; for the fear of the YAHAWAH came upon them: and they spoiled all the cities; for there was exceeding much spoil in them.
They smote also the tents of cattle, and carried away sheep and camels in abundance, and returned to Yerushalayim.
And the Ruwach of ELOHIYM came upon AzarYah the son of Oded:

And he went out to meet Asa, and said unto him, Hear ye me, Asa, and all Yehuda and Benyamin; The YAHAWAH is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you.
Now for a long season YisraEL hath been without the true ELOHIYM, and without a teaching priest, and without law.
But when they in their trouble did turn unto the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of YisraEL, and sought him, he was found of them.
And in those times there was no peace to him that went out, nor to him that came in, but great vexations were upon all the inhabitants of the countries.
And nation was destroyed of nation, and city of city: for ELOHIYM did vex them with all adversity.
Be ye strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.

And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Yehuda and Benyamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim, and renewed the altar of the YAHAWAH, that was before the porch of the YAHAWAH.

And he gathered all Yehuda and Benyamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of YisraEL in abundance, when they saw that the YAHAWAH his ELOHIYM was with him.
So they gathered themselves together at Yerushalayim in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.
And they offered unto the YAHAWAH the same time, of the spoil which they had brought, seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.
And they entered into a covenant to seek the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul;
That whosoever would not seek the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of YisraEL should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.
And they sware unto the YAHAWAH with a loud voice, and with shouting, and with trumpets, and with cornets.
And all Yehuda praised at the oath: for they had sworn with all their heart, and sought him with their whole desire; and he was found of them: and the YAHAWAH gave them rest round about.

¶ And also concerning Maachah the mother of Asa the king, he removed her from being queen, because she had made an idol in a grove: and Asa cut down her idol, and stamped it, and burnt it at the brook Kidron.
But the high places were not taken away out of YisraEL: nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect all his days.
¶ And he brought into the house of ELOHIYM the things that his father had dedicated, and that he himself had dedicated, silver, and gold, and vessels.
And there was no more war unto the five and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa.
In the six and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa Baasha king of YisraEL came up against Yehuda, and built Ramah, to the intent that he might let none go out or come in to Asa king of Yehuda.
Then Asa brought out silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of the YAHAWAH and of the king’s house, and sent to Ben-hadad king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,

There is a league between me and thee, as there was between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent thee silver and gold; go, break thy league with Baasha king of YisraEL, that he may depart from me.
And Ben-hadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of YisraEL; and they smote Iyyon, and Dan, and Abelmaim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.
And it came to pass, when Baasha heard it, that he left off building of Ramah, and let his work cease.
Then Asa the king took all Yehuda; and they carried away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha was building; and he built therewith Geba and Mizpah.

¶ And at that time YOHANANi the seer came to Asa king of Yehuda, and said unto him, Because thou hast relied on the king of Syria, and not relied on the YAHAWAH thy ELOHIYM, therefore is the host of the king of Syria escaped out of thine hand.
Were not the Ethiopians and the Lubims a huge host, with very many chariots and horsemen? yet, because thou didst rely on the YAHAWAH, he delivered them into thine hand.

For the eyes of the YAHAWAH run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.
Then Asa was wroth with the seer, and put him in a prison house; for he was in a rage with him because of this thing. And Asa oppressed some of the people the same time.
¶ And, behold, the acts of Asa, first and last, lo, they are written in the book of the kings of Yehuda and YisraEL.
And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to the YAHAWAH, but to the physicians.
¶ And Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the one and fortieth year of his reign.

And they buried him in his own sepulchres, which he had made for himself in the city of David, and laid him in the bed which was filled with sweet odours and divers kinds of spices prepared by the apothecaries’ art: and they made a very great burning for him.
And YEHOSHUAphat his son reigned in his stead, and strengthened himself against YisraEL.
And he placed forces in all the fenced cities of Yehuda, and set garrisons in the land of Yehuda, and in the cities of Ephraim, which Asa his father had taken.
And the YAHAWAH was with YEHOSHUAphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father David, and sought not unto Baalim;
But sought to the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of YisraEL.
Therefore the YAHAWAH stablished the kingdom in his hand; and all Yehuda brought to YEHOSHUAphat presents; and he had riches and honor in abundance.
And his heart was lifted up in the ways of the YAHAWAH: moreover he took away the high places and groves out of Yehuda.
¶ Also in the third year of his reign he sent to his princes, even to Benhail, and to ObadYah, and to ZecharYah, and to Nethaneel, and to MichaYah, to teach in the cities of Yehuda.

And with them he sent Levites, even ShemaYah, and NethanYah, and ZebadYah, and Asahel, and Shemiramoth, and Yehonathan, and AdoniYah, and TobiYah, and TobadoniYah, Levites; and with them Elishama and Yehoram, priests.
And they taught in Yehuda, and had the book of the law of the YAHAWAH with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Yehuda, and taught the people.
¶ And the fear of the YAHAWAH fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were round about Yehuda, so that they made no war against YEHOSHUAphat.

Also some of the Philistines brought YEHOSHUAphat presents, and tribute silver; and the Arabians brought him flocks, seven thousand and seven hundred rams, and seven thousand and seven hundred he goats.
¶ And YEHOSHUAphat waxed great exceedingly; and he built in Yehuda castles, and cities of store.
And he had much business in the cities of Yehuda: and the men of war, mighty men of valour, were in Yerushalayim.
And these are the numbers of them according to the house of their fathers: Of Yehuda, the captains of thousands; Adnah the chief, and with him mighty men of valour three hundred thousand.
And next to him was YehoYOHANAN the captain, and with him two hundred and fourscore thousand.
And next him was AmasYah the son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself unto the YAHAWAH; and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valour.
And of Benyamin; Eliada a mighty man of valour, and with him armed men with bow and shield two hundred thousand.
And next him was Yehozabad, and with him an hundred and fourscore thousand ready prepared for the war.
These waited on the king, beside those whom the king put in the fenced cities throughout all Yehuda.
Now YEHOSHUAphat had riches and honor in abundance, and united affinity with Ahab.

And after certain years he went down to Ahab to Samaria. And Ahab killed sheep and oxen for him in abundance, and for the people that he had with him, and persuaded him to go up with him to Ramoth-gilead.

And Ahab king of YisraEL said unto YEHOSHUAphat king of Yehuda, Wilt thou go with me to Ramoth-gilead? And he answered him, I am as thou art, and my people as thy people; and we will be with thee in the war.
¶ And YEHOSHUAphat said unto the king of YisraEL, Enquire, I pray thee, at the word of the YAHAWAH to day.

Therefore the king of YisraEL gathered together of prophets four hundred men, and said unto them, Shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And they said, Go up; for ELOHIYM will deliver it into the king’s hand.
But YEHOSHUAphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the YAHAWAH besides, that we might enquire of him?

And the king of YisraEL said unto YEHOSHUAphat, There is yet one man, by whom we may enquire of the YAHAWAH: but I hate him; for he never prophesied good unto me, but always evil: the same is MicaYah the son of Imla. And YEHOSHUAphat said, Let not the king say so.
And the king of YisraEL called for one of his officers, and said, Fetch quickly MicaYah the son of Imla.

And the king of YisraEL and YEHOSHUAphat king of Yehuda sat either of them on his throne, clothed in their robes, and they sat in a void place at the entering in of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets prophesied before them.
And ZedekYah the son of Chenaanah had made him horns of iron, and said, Thus saith the YAHAWAH, With these thou shalt push Syria until they be consumed.
And all the prophets prophesied so, saying, Go up to Ramoth-gilead, and prosper: for the YAHAWAH shall deliver it into the hand of the king.

And the messenger that went to call MicaYah spake to him, saying, Behold, the words of the prophets declare good to the king with one assent; let thy word therefore, I pray thee, be like one of their’s, and speak thou good.
And MicaYah said, As the YAHAWAH liveth, even what my ELOHIYM saith, that will I speak.

And when he was come to the king, the king said unto him, MicaYah, shall we go to Ramothgilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And he said, Go ye up, and prosper, and they shall be delivered into your hand.
And the king said to him, How many times shall I urge thee that thou say nothing but the truth to me in the name of the YAHAWAH?

Then he said, I did see all YisraEL scattered upon the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd: and the YAHAWAH said, These have no master; let them return therefore every man to his house in peace.
And the king of YisraEL said to YEHOSHUAphat, Did I not tell thee that he would not prophesy good unto me, but evil?
Again he said, Therefore hear the word of the YAHAWAH; I saw the YAHAWAH sitting upon his throne, and all the host of heaven standing on his right hand and on his left.
And the YAHAWAH said, Who shall entice Ahab king of YisraEL, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead? And one spake saying after this manner, and another saying after that manner.
Then there came out a spirit, and stood before the YAHAWAH, and said, I will entice him. And the YAHAWAH said unto him, Wherewith?
And he said, I will go out, and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And the YAHAWAH said, Thou shalt entice him, and thou shalt also prevail: go out, and do even so.
Now therefore, behold, the YAHAWAH hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of these thy prophets, and the YAHAWAH hath spoken evil against thee.
Then ZedekYah the son of Chenaanah came near, and smote MicaYah upon the cheek, and said, Which way went the Spirit of the YAHAWAH from me to speak unto thee?
And MicaYah said, Behold, thou shalt see on that day when thou shalt go into an inner chamber to hide thyself.
Then the king of YisraEL said, Take ye MicaYah, and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city, and to Yo’ash the king’s son;
And say, Thus saith the king, Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I return in peace.
And MicaYah said, If thou certainly return in peace, then hath not the YAHAWAH spoken by me. And he said, Hearken, all ye people.
So the king of YisraEL and YEHOSHUAphat the king of Yehuda went up to Ramoth-gilead.
And the king of YisraEL said unto YEHOSHUAphat, I will disguise myself, and will go to the battle; but put thou on thy robes. So the king of YisraEL disguised himself; and they went to the battle.
Now the king of Syria had commanded the captains of the chariots that were with him, saying, Fight ye not with small or great, save only with the king of YisraEL.

And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw YEHOSHUAphat, that they said, It is the king of YisraEL. Therefore they compassed about him to fight: but YEHOSHUAphat cried out, and the YAHAWAH helped him; and ELOHIYM moved them to depart from him.
For it came to pass, that, when the captains of the chariots perceived that it was not the king of YisraEL, they turned back again from pursuing him.

And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of YisraEL between the connections of the harness: therefore he said to his chariot man, Turn thine hand, that thou mayest carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.
And the battle increased that day: howbeit the king of YisraEL stayed himself up in his chariot against the Syrians until the even: and about the time of the sun going down he died.
And YEHOSHUAphat the king of Yehuda returned to his house in peace to Yerushalayim.

And Yehu the son of YOHANANi the seer went out to meet him, and said to king YEHOSHUAphat, Shouldest thou help the unrighteous, and love them that hate the YAHAWAH? therefore is wrath upon thee from before the YAHAWAH.
Nevertheless there are good things found in thee, in that thou hast taken away the groves out of the land, and hast prepared thine heart to seek ELOHIYM.
And YEHOSHUAphat dwelt at Yerushalayim: and he went out again through the people from Beersheba to mount Ephraim, and brought them back unto the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of their fathers.
¶ And he set magistrates in the land throughout all the fenced cities of Yehuda, city by city,
And said to the magistrates, Take heed what ye do: for ye magistrate not for man, but for the YAHAWAH, who is with you in the mishpat.
Wherefore now let the fear of the YAHAWAH be upon you; take heed and do it: for there is no iniquity with the YAHAWAH our ELOHIYM, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts.

¶ Moreover in Yerushalayim did YEHOSHUAphat set of the Levites, and of the priests, and of the chief of the fathers of YisraEL, for the mishpat of the YAHAWAH, and for controversies, when they returned to Yerushalayim.
And he charged them, saying, Thus shall ye do in the fear of the YAHAWAH, faithfully, and with a perfect heart.

And what cause soever shall come to you of your brethren that dwell in their cities, between blood and blood, between law and commandment, statutes and mishpats, ye shall even warn them that they trespass not against the YAHAWAH, and so wrath come upon you, and upon your brethren: this do, and ye shall not trespass.

And, behold, AmarYah the chief priest is over you in all matters of the YAHAWAH; and ZebadYah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Yehuda, for all the king’s matters: also the Levites shall be officers before you. Deal courageously, and the YAHAWAH shall be with the good.
It came to pass after this also, that the children of Moab, and the children of Ammon, and with them other beside the Ammonites, came against YEHOSHUAphat to battle.
Then there came some that told YEHOSHUAphat, saying, There cometh a great multitude against thee from beyond the sea on this side Syria; and, behold, they be in Hazazon-tamar, which is En-gedi.
And YEHOSHUAphat feared, and set himself to seek the YAHAWAH, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Yehuda.
And Yehuda gathered themselves together, to ask help of the YAHAWAH: even out of all the cities of Yehuda they came to seek the YAHAWAH.
¶ And YEHOSHUAphat stood in the congregation of Yehuda and Yerushalayim, in the house of the YAHAWAH, before the new court,

And said, O YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of our fathers, art not thou ELOHIYM in heaven? and rulest not thou over all the kingdoms of the heathen? and in thine hand is there not power and might, so that none is able to withstand thee?
Art not thou our ELOHIYM, who didst drive out the inhabitants of this land before thy people YisraEL, and gavest it to the seed of Abraham thy friend for ever?
And they dwelt therein, and have built thee a sanctuary therein for thy name, saying,

If, when evil cometh upon us, as the sword, shephowt (punishment), or pestilence, or famine, we stand before this house, and in thy presence, (for thy name is in this house,) and cry unto thee in our affliction, then thou wilt hear and help.
And now, behold, the children of Ammon and Moab and mount Seir, whom thou wouldest not let YisraEL invade, when they came out of the land of Egypt, but they turned from them, and destroyed them not;
Behold, I say, how they reward us, to come to cast us out of thy possession, which thou hast given us to inherit.
O our ELOHIYM, wilt thou not magistrate them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.
And all Yehuda stood before the YAHAWAH, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
¶ Then upon Yahaziel the son of ZecharYah, the son of BenaYah, the son of Yei’el, the son of MattanYah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, came the Ruwach of the YAHAWAH in the midst of the congregation;

And he said, Hearken ye, all Yehuda, and ye inhabitants of Yerushalayim, and thou king YEHOSHUAphat, Thus saith the YAHAWAH unto you, Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not your’s, but ELOHIYM’S.
To morrow go ye down against them: behold, they come up by the cliff of Ziz; and ye shall find them at the end of the brook, before the wilderness of Yeru’el.

Ye shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the YAHAWAH with you, O Yehuda and Yerushalayim: fear not, nor be dismayed; to morrow go out against them: for the YAHAWAH will be with you.
And YEHOSHUAphat bowed his head with his face to the ground: and all Yehuda and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim fell before the YAHAWAH, worshipping the YAHAWAH.
And the Levites, of the children of the Kohathites, and of the children of the Korhites, stood up to praise the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of YisraEL with a loud voice on high.

¶ And they rose early in the morning, and went forth into the wilderness of Tekoa: and as they went forth, YEHOSHUAphat stood and said, Hear me, O Yehuda, and ye inhabitants of Yerushalayim; Believe in the YAHAWAH your ELOHIYM, so shall ye be established; believe his prophets, so shall ye prosper.

And when he had consulted with the people, he appointed singers unto the YAHAWAH, and that should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army, and to say, Praise the YAHAWAH; for his mercy endureth for ever.
¶ And when they began to sing and to praise, the YAHAWAH set ambushments against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, which were come against Yehuda; and they were smitten.

For the children of Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants of mount Seir, utterly to slay and destroy them: and when they had made an end of the inhabitants of Seir, every one helped to destroy another.
And when Yehuda came toward the watch tower in the wilderness, they looked unto the multitude, and, behold, they were dead bodies fallen to the earth, and none escaped.

And when YEHOSHUAphat and his people came to take away the spoil of them, they found among them in abundance both riches with the dead bodies, and precious keli, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could carry away: and they were three days in gathering of the spoil, it was so much.

¶ And on the fourth day they assembled themselves in the valley of Berachah; for there they barakat the YAHAWAH: therefore the name of the same place was called, The valley of Berachah, unto this day.

Then they returned, every man of Yehuda and Yerushalayim, and YEHOSHUAphat in the forefront of them, to go again to Yerushalayim with delight; for the YAHAWAH had made them to triumph over their enemies.
And they came to Yerushalayim with psalteries and harps and trumpets unto the house of the YAHAWAH.
And the fear of ELOHIYM was on all the kingdoms of those countries, when they had heard that the YAHAWAH fought against the enemies of YisraEL.
So the realm of YEHOSHUAphat was quiet: for his ELOHIYM gave him rest round about.

¶ And YEHOSHUAphat reigned over Yehuda: he was thirty and five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty and five years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.
And he walked in the way of Asa his father, and departed not from it, doing that which was right in the sight of the YAHAWAH.
Howbeit the high places were not taken away: for as yet the people had not prepared their hearts unto the ELOHIYM of their fathers.
Now the rest of the acts of YEHOSHUAphat, first and last, behold, they are written in the book of Yehu the son of YOHANANi, who is mentioned in the book of the kings of YisraEL.
¶ And after this did YEHOSHUAphat king of Yehuda unite himself with AhazYah king of YisraEL, who did very wickedly:
And he united himself with him to make ships to go to Tarshish: and they made the ships in Ezion-geber.

Then Eliezer the son of Dodavah of Mareshah prophesied against YEHOSHUAphat, saying, Because thou hast united thyself with AhazYah, the YAHAWAH hath broken thy works. And the ships were broken, that they were not able to go to Tarshish.
Now YEHOSHUAphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And Yehoram his son reigned in his stead.
And he had brethren the sons of YEHOSHUAphat, AzarYah, and Yei’el, and ZecharYah, and AzarYah, and Michael, and ShephatYah: all these were the sons of YEHOSHUAphat king of YisraEL.
And their father gave them great gifts of silver, and of gold, and of precious things, with fenced cities in Yehuda: but the kingdom gave he to Yehoram; because he was the firstborn.
Now when Yehoram was risen up to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself, and slew all his brethren with the sword, and divers also of the princes of YisraEL.
¶ Yehoram was thirty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Yerushalayim.
And he walked in the way of the kings of YisraEL, like as did the house of Ahab: for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife: and he wrought that which was evil in the eyes of the YAHAWAH.
Howbeit the YAHAWAH would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he promised to give a light to him and to his sons for ever.
¶ In his days the Edomites revolted from under the dominion of Yehuda, and made themselves a king.
Then Yehoram went forth with his princes, and all his chariots with him: and he rose up by night, and smote the Edomites which compassed him in, and the captains of the chariots.
So the Edomites revolted from under the hand of Yehuda unto this day. The same time also did Libnah revolt from under his hand; because he had forsaken the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of his fathers.
Moreover he made high places in the mountains of Yehuda, and caused the inhabitants of Yerushalayim to commit fornication, and compelled Yehuda thereto.

¶ And there came a writing to him from EliYahu the prophet, saying, Thus saith the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of David thy father, Because thou hast not walked in the ways of YEHOSHUAphat thy father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Yehuda,

But hast walked in the way of the kings of YisraEL, and hast made Yehuda and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim to go a whoring, like to the whoredoms of the house of Ahab, and also hast slain thy brethren of thy father’s house, which were better than thyself:
Behold, with a great plague will the YAHAWAH smite thy people, and thy children, and thy wives, and all thy goods:
And thou shalt have great sickness by disease of thy bowels, until thy bowels fall out by reason of the sickness day by day.
¶ Moreover the YAHAWAH stirred up against Yehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians, that were near the Ethiopians:

And they came up into Yehuda, and brake into it, and carried away all the substance that was found in the king’s house, and his sons also, and his wives; so that there was never a son left him, save Yeho’ahaz, the youngest of his sons.
¶ And after all this the YAHAWAH smote him in his bowels with an incurable disease.

And it came to pass, that in process of time, after the end of two years, his bowels fell out by reason of his sickness: so he died of sore diseases. And his people made no burning for him, like the burning of his fathers.

Thirty and two years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned in Yerushalayim eight years, and departed without being desired. Howbeit they buried him in the city of David, but not in the sepulchres of the kings.

And the inhabitants of Yerushalayim made AhazYah his youngest son king in his stead: for the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest. So AhazYah the son of Yehoram king of Yehuda reigned.
Forty and two years old was AhazYah when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Yerushalayim. His mother’s name also was AthalYah the daughter of Omri.
He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly.
Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the YAHAWAH like the house of Ahab: for they were his counsellors after the death of his father to his destruction.
¶ He walked also after their counsel, and went with Yehoram the son of Ahab king of YisraEL to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead: and the Syrians smote Yoram.

And he returned to be healed in Yizre’el because of the wounds which were given him at Ramah, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria. And AzarYah the son of Yehoram king of Yehuda went down to see Yehoram the son of Ahab at Yizre’el, because he was sick.

And the destruction of AhazYah was of ELOHIYM by coming to Yoram: for when he was come, he went out with Yehoram against Yehu the son of Nimshi, whom the YAHAWAH had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
And it came to pass, that, when Yehu was executing sentence upon the house of Ahab, and found the princes of Yehuda, and the sons of the brethren of AhazYah, that ministered to AhazYah, he slew them.

And he sought AhazYah: and they caught him, (for he was hid in Samaria,) and brought him to Yehu: and when they had slain him, they buried him: Because, said they, he is the son of YEHOSHUAphat, who sought the YAHAWAH with all his heart. So the house of AhazYah had no power to keep still the kingdom.
¶ But when AthalYah the mother of AhazYah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Yehuda.

But Yehosab’at, the daughter of the king, took Yo’ash the son of AhazYah, and stole him from among the king’s sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Yehosab’at, the daughter of king Yehoram, the wife of Yehoyada the priest, (for she was the sister of AhazYah,) hid him from AthalYah, so that she slew him not.
And he was with them hid in the house of ELOHIYM six years: and AthalYah reigned over the land.

And in the seventh year Yehoyada strengthened himself, and took the captains of hundreds, AzarYah the son of Yeroham, and Ishmael the son of YehoYOHANAN, and AzarYah the son of Obed, and MaaseYah the son of AdaYah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri, into covenant with him.
And they went about in Yehuda, and gathered the Levites out of all the cities of Yehuda, and the chief of the fathers of YisraEL, and they came to Yerushalayim.
And all the congregation made a covenant with the king in the house of ELOHIYM. And he said unto them, Behold, the king’s son shall reign, as the YAHAWAH hath said of the sons of David.
This is the thing that ye shall do; A third part of you entering on the Sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, shall be porters of the doors;
And a third part shall be at the king’s house; and a third part at the gate of the foundation: and all the people shall be in the courts of the house of the YAHAWAH.
But let none come into the house of the YAHAWAH, save the priests, and they that minister of the Levites; they shall go in, for they are holy: but all the people shall keep the watch of the YAHAWAH.

And the Levites shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand; and whosoever else cometh into the house, he shall be put to death: but be ye with the king when he cometh in, and when he goeth out.

So the Levites and all Yehuda did according to all things that Yehoyada the priest had commanded, and took every man his men that were to come in on the Sabbath, with them that were to go out on the Sabbath: for Yehoyada the priest dismissed not the courses.
Moreover Yehoyada the priest delivered to the captains of hundreds spears, and bucklers, and shields, that had been King David’s, which were in the house of ELOHIYM.
And he set all the people, every man having his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the temple to the left side of the temple, along by the altar and the temple, by the king round about.
Then they brought out the king’s son, and put upon him the crown, and gave him the testimony, and made him king. And Yehoyada and his sons anointed him, and said, ELOHIYM save the king.
¶ Now when AthalYah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people into the house of the YAHAWAH:

And she looked, and, behold, the king stood at his pillar at the entering in, and the princes and the trumpets by the king: and all the people of the land praised, and sounded with trumpets, also the singers with instruments of musick, and such as taught to sing praise. Then AthalYah rent her clothes, and said, Treason, Treason.

Then Yehoyada the priest brought out the captains of hundreds that were set over the host, and said unto them, Have her forth of the ranges: and whoso followeth her, let him be slain with the sword. For the priest said, Slay her not in the house of the YAHAWAH.
So they laid hands on her; and when she was come to the entering of the horse gate by the king’s house, they slew her there.
¶ And Yehoyada made a covenant between him, and between all the people, and between the king, that they should be the YAHAWAH’S people.
Then all the people went to the house of Baal, and brake it down, and brake his altars and his images in pieces, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars.

Also Yehoyada appointed the offices of the house of the YAHAWAH by the hand of the priests the Levites, whom David had distributed in the house of the YAHAWAH, to offer the burnt offerings of the YAHAWAH as it is written in the law of Moses, with praising and with singing, as it was ordained by David.
And he set the porters at the gates of the house of the YAHAWAH, that none which was unclean in any thing should enter in.

And he took the captains of hundreds, and the nobles, and the governors of the people, and all the people of the land, and brought down the king from the house of the YAHAWAH: and they came through the high gate into the king’s house, and set the king upon the throne of the kingdom.
And all the people of the land praised: and the city was quiet, after that they had slain AthalYah with the sword.
Yo’ash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Yerushalayim. His mother’s name also was ZibYah of Beer-sheba.
And Yo’ash did that which was right in the sight of the YAHAWAH all the days of Yehoyada the priest.
And Yehoyada took for him two wives; and he begat sons and daughters.
¶ And it came to pass after this, that Yo’ash was minded to repair the house of the YAHAWAH.

And he gathered together the priests and the Levites, and said to them, Go out unto the cities of Yehuda, and gather of all YisraEL money to repair the house of your ELOHIYM from year to year, and see that ye hasten the matter. Howbeit the Levites hastened it not.

And the king called for Yehoyada the chief, and said unto him, Why hast thou not required of the Levites to bring in out of Yehuda and out of Yerushalayim the collection, according to the commandment of Moses the servant of the YAHAWAH, and of the congregation of YisraEL, for the tabernacle of witness?
For the sons of AthalYah, that wicked woman, had broken up the house of ELOHIYM; and also all the dedicated things of the house of the YAHAWAH did they bestow upon Baalim.
And at the king’s commandment they made a chest, and set it without at the gate of the house of the YAHAWAH.
And they made a proclamation through Yehuda and Yerushalayim, to bring in to the YAHAWAH the collection that Moses the servant of ELOHIYM laid upon YisraEL in the wilderness.
And all the princes and all the people praised, and brought in, and cast into the chest, until they had made an end.

Now it came to pass, that at what time the chest was brought unto the king’s office by the hand of the Levites, and when they saw that there was much money, the king’s scribe and the high priest’s officer came and emptied the chest, and took it, and carried it to his place again. Thus they did day by day, and gathered money in abundance.

And the king and Yehoyada gave it to such as did the work of the service of the house of the YAHAWAH, and hired masons and carpenters to repair the house of the YAHAWAH, and also such as wrought iron and brass to mend the house of the YAHAWAH.
So the workmen wrought, and the work was perfected by them, and they set the house of ELOHIYM in his state, and strengthened it.

And when they had finished it, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Yehoyada, whereof were made vessels for the house of the YAHAWAH, even vessels to minister, and to offer withal, and spoons, and vessels of gold and silver. And they offered burnt offerings in the house of the YAHAWAH continually all the days of Yehoyada.
¶ But Yehoyada waxed old, and was full of days when he died; an hundred and thirty years old was he when he died.
And they buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in YisraEL, both toward ELOHIYM, and toward his house.
Now after the death of Yehoyada came the princes of Yehuda, and made obeisance to the king. Then the king hearkened unto them.
And they left the house of the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of their fathers, and served groves and idols: and wrath came upon Yehuda and Yerushalayim for this their trespass.
Yet he sent prophets to them, to bring them again unto the YAHAWAH; and they testified against them: but they would not give ear.

And the Ruwach of ELOHIYM came upon ZecharYah the son of Yehoyada the priest, which stood above the people, and said unto them, Thus saith ELOHIYM, Why transgress ye the commandments of the YAHAWAH, that ye cannot prosper? because ye have forsaken the YAHAWAH, he hath also forsaken you.
And they conspired against him, and stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king in the court of the house of the YAHAWAH.
Thus Yo’ash the king remembered not the kindness which Yehoyada his father had done to him, but slew his son. And when he died, he said, The YAHAWAH look upon it, and require it.

¶ And it came to pass at the end of the year, that the host of Syria came up against him: and they came to Yehuda and Yerushalayim, and destroyed all the princes of the people from among the people, and sent all the spoil of them unto the king of Damascus.

For the army of the Syrians came with a small company of men, and the YAHAWAH delivered a very great host into their hand, because they had forsaken the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of their fathers. So they executed shephet against Yo’ash.

And when they were departed from him, (for they left him in great diseases,) his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Yehoyada the priest, and slew him on his bed, and he died: and they buried him in the city of David, but they buried him not in the sepulchres of the kings.
And these are they that conspired against him; Zabad the son of Shimeath an Ammonitess, and Yehozabad the son of Shimrith a Moabitess.

¶ Now concerning his sons, and the greatness of the burdens laid upon him, and the repairing of the house of ELOHIYM, behold, they are written in the story of the book of the kings. And AmazYah his son reigned in his stead.
AmazYah was twenty and five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty and nine years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Yeho’addin of Yerushalayim.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the YAHAWAH, but not with a perfect heart.
¶ Now it came to pass, when the kingdom was established to him, that he slew his servants that had killed the king his father.

But he slew not their children, but did as it is written in the law in the book of Moses, where the YAHAWAH commanded, saying, The fathers shall not die for the children, neither shall the children die for the fathers, but every man shall die for his own sin.

¶ Moreover AmazYah gathered Yehuda together, and made them captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, according to the houses of their fathers, throughout all Yehuda and Benyamin: and he numbered them from twenty years old and above, and found them three hundred thousand choice men, able to go forth to war, that could handle spear and shield.
He hired also an hundred thousand mighty men of valour out of YisraEL for an hundred talents of silver.
But there came a man of ELOHIYM to him, saying, O king, let not the army of YisraEL go with thee; for the YAHAWAH is not with YisraEL, to wit, with all the children of Ephraim.
But if thou wilt go, do it, be strong for the battle: ELOHIYM shall make thee fall before the enemy: for ELOHIYM hath power to help, and to cast down.

And AmazYah said to the man of ELOHIYM, But what shall we do for the hundred talents which I have given to the army of YisraEL? And the man of ELOHIYM answered, The YAHAWAH is able to give thee much more than this.
Then AmazYah separated them, to wit, the army that was come to him out of Ephraim, to go home again: wherefore their anger was greatly kindled against Yehuda, and they returned home in great anger.
¶ And AmazYah strengthened himself, and led forth his people, and went to the valley of salt, and smote of the children of Seir ten thousand.

And other ten thousand left alive did the children of Yehuda carry away captive, and brought them unto the top of the rock, and cast them down from the top of the rock, that they all were broken in pieces.

¶ But the soldiers of the army which AmazYah sent back, that they should not go with him to battle, fell upon the cities of Yehuda, from Samaria even unto Beth-horon, and smote three thousand of them, and took much spoil.

¶ Now it came to pass, after that AmazYah was come from the slaughter of the Edomites, that he brought the deities of the children of Seir, and set them up to be his elohiyms, and bowed down himself before them, and burned incense unto them.

Wherefore the anger of the YAHAWAH was kindled against AmazYah, and he sent unto him a prophet, which said unto him, Why hast thou sought after the elohiyms of the people, which could not deliver their own people out of thine hand?

And it came to pass, as he talked with him, that the king said unto him, Art thou made of the king’s counsel? forbear; why shouldest thou be smitten? Then the prophet forbare, and said, I know that ELOHIYM hath determined to destroy thee, because thou hast done this, and hast not hearkened unto my counsel.
¶ Then AmazYah king of Yehuda took advice, and sent to Yo’ash, the son of Yeho’ahaz, the son of Yehu, king of YisraEL, saying, Come, let us see one another in the face.

And Yo’ash king of YisraEL sent to AmazYah king of Yehuda, saying, The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, Give thy daughter to my son to wife: and there passed by a wild beast that was in Lebanon, and trode down the thistle.

Thou sayest, Lo, thou hast smitten the Edomites; and thine heart lifteth thee up to boast: abide now at home; why shouldest thou meddle to thine hurt, that thou shouldest fall, even thou, and Yehuda with thee?
But AmazYah would not hear; for it came of ELOHIYM, that he might deliver them into the hand of their enemies, because they sought after the deities of Edom.
So Yo’ash the king of YisraEL went up; and they saw one another in the face, both he and AmazYah king of Yehuda, at Beth-shemesh, which belongeth to Yehuda.
And Yehuda was put to the worse before YisraEL, and they fled every man to his tent.

And Yo’ash the king of YisraEL took AmazYah king of Yehuda, the son of Yo’ash, the son of Yeho’ahaz, at Beth-shemesh, and brought him to Yerushalayim, and brake down the wall of Yerushalayim from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits.
And he took all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of ELOHIYM with Obed-edom, and the treasures of the king’s house, the hostages also, and returned to Samaria.
¶ And AmazYah the son of Yo’ash king of Yehuda lived after the death of Yo’ash son of Yeho’ahaz king of YisraEL fifteen years.
Now the rest of the acts of AmazYah, first and last, behold, are they not written in the book of the kings of Yehuda and YisraEL?

¶ Now after the time that AmazYah did turn away from following the YAHAWAH they made a conspiracy against him in Yerushalayim; and he fled to Lachish: but they sent to Lachish after him, and slew him there.
And they brought him upon horses, and buried him with his fathers in the city of Yehuda.
Then all the people of Yehuda took UzzYah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father AmazYah.
He built Eloth, and restored it to Yehuda, after that the king slept with his fathers.
Sixteen years old was UzzYah when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty and two years in Yerushalayim. His mother’s name also was Yekolya of Yerushalayim.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the YAHAWAH, according to all that his father AmazYah did.
And he sought ELOHIYM in the days of ZecharYah, who had understanding in the visions of ELOHIYM: and as long as he sought the YAHAWAH, ELOHIYM made him to prosper.
And he went forth and warred against the Philistines, and brake down the wall of Gath, and the wall of Yavneh, and the wall of Ashdod, and built cities about Ashdod, and among the Philistines.
And ELOHIYM helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians that dwelt in Gurbaal, and the Mehunims.
And the Ammonites gave gifts to UzzYah: and his name spread abroad even to the entering in of Egypt; for he strengthened himself exceedingly.
Moreover UzzYah built towers in Yerushalayim at the corner gate, and at the valley gate, and at the turning of the wall, and fortified them.

Also he built towers in the desert, and digged many wells: for he had much cattle, both in the low country, and in the plains: husbandmen also, and vine dressers in the mountains, and in Carmel: for he loved husbandry.

Moreover UzzYah had an host of fighting men, that went out to war by bands, according to the number of their account by the hand of Yei’el the scribe and MaaseYah the ruler, under the hand of YOHANANYah, one of the king’s captains.
The whole number of the chief of the fathers of the mighty men of valour were two thousand and six hundred.
And under their hand was an army, three hundred thousand and seven thousand and five hundred, that made war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.
And UzzYah prepared for them throughout all the host shields, and spears, and helmets, and habergeons, and bows, and slings to cast stones.

And he made in Yerushalayim engines, invented by cunning men, to be on the towers and upon the bulwarks, to shoot arrows and great stones withal. And his name spread far abroad; for he was marvellously helped, till he was strong.

¶ But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against the YAHAWAH his ELOHIYM, and went into the temple of the YAHAWAH to burn incense upon the altar of incense.
And AzarYah the priest went in after him, and with him fourscore priests of the YAHAWAH, that were valiant men:

And they withstood UzzYah the king, and said unto him, It appertaineth not unto thee, UzzYah, to burn incense unto the YAHAWAH, but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed; neither shall it be for thine honor from the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM.

Then UzzYah was wroth, and had a censer in his hand to burn incense: and while he was wroth with the priests, the leprosy even rose up in his forehead before the priests in the house of the YAHAWAH, from beside the incense altar.

And AzarYah the chief priest, and all the priests, looked upon him, and, behold, he was leprous in his forehead, and they thrust him out from thence; yea, himself hasted also to go out, because the YAHAWAH had smitten him.

And UzzYah the king was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a several house, being a leper; for he was cut off from the house of the YAHAWAH: and Yotam his son was over the king’s house, arbitrating the people of the land.
¶ Now the rest of the acts of UzzYah, first and last, did Ysha’yah the prophet, the son of Amoz, write.
So UzzYah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of the burial which belonged to the kings; for they said, He is a leper: and Yotam his son reigned in his stead.
Yotam was twenty and five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim. His mother’s name also was Yerushah, the daughter of Zadok.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the YAHAWAH, according to all that his father UzzYah did: howbeit he entered not into the temple of the YAHAWAH. And the people did yet corruptly.
He built the high gate of the house of the YAHAWAH, and on the wall of Ophel he built much.
Moreover he built cities in the mountains of Yehuda, and in the forests he built castles and towers.

¶ He fought also with the king of the Ammonites, and prevailed against them. And the children of Ammon gave him the same year an hundred talents of silver, and ten thousand measures of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. So much did the children of Ammon pay unto him, both the second year, and the third.
So Yotam became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the YAHAWAH his ELOHIYM.
¶ Now the rest of the acts of Yotam, and all his wars, and his ways, lo, they are written in the book of the kings of YisraEL and Yehuda.
He was five and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim.
¶ And Yotam slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David: and Ahaz his son reigned in his stead.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim: but he did not that which was right in the sight of the YAHAWAH, like David his father:
For he walked in the ways of the kings of YisraEL, and made also molten images for Baalim.
Moreover he burnt incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and burnt his children in the fire, after the abominations of the heathen whom the YAHAWAH had cast out before the children of YisraEL.
He sacrificed also and burnt incense in the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree.

Wherefore the YAHAWAH his ELOHIYM delivered him into the hand of the king of Syria; and they smote him, and carried away a great multitude of them captives, and brought them to Damascus. And he was also delivered into the hand of the king of YisraEL, who smote him with a great slaughter.
¶ For Pekah the son of RemalYah slew in Yehuda an hundred and twenty thousand in one day, which were all valiant men; because they had forsaken the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of their fathers.
And Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, slew MaaseYah the king’s son, and Azrikam the governor of the house, and Elkanah that was next to the king.
And the children of YisraEL carried away captive of their brethren two hundred thousand, women, sons, and daughters, and took also away much spoil from them, and brought the spoil to Samaria.

But a prophet of the YAHAWAH was there, whose name was Oded: and he went out before the host that came to Samaria, and said unto them, Behold, because the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of your fathers was wroth with Yehuda, he hath delivered them into your hand, and ye have slain them in a rage that reacheth up unto heaven.
And now ye purpose to keep under the children of Yehuda and Yerushalayim for bondmen and bondwomen unto you: but are there not with you, even with you, sins against the YAHAWAH your ELOHIYM?
Now hear me therefore, and deliver the captives again, which ye have taken captive of your brethren: for the fierce wrath of the YAHAWAH is upon you.

Then certain of the heads of the children of Ephraim, AzarYah the son of YocYOHANAN, BerechYah the son of Meshillemoth, and YehizkYah the son of Shallum, and Amasa the son of Hadlai, stood up against them that came from the war,

And said unto them, Ye shall not bring in the captives hither: for whereas we have offended against the YAHAWAH already, ye intend to add more to our sins and to our trespass: for our trespass is great, and there is fierce wrath against YisraEL.
So the armed men left the captives and the spoil before the princes and all the congregation.

And the men which were expressed by name rose up, and took the captives, and with the spoil clothed all that were naked among them, and arrayed them, and shod them, and gave them to eat and to drink, and anointed them, and carried all the feeble of them upon asses, and brought them to Yeriho, the city of palm trees, to their brethren: then they returned to Samaria.
¶ At that time did king Ahaz send unto the kings of Assyria to help him.
For again the Edomites had come and smitten Yehuda, and carried away captives.

The Philistines also had invaded the cities of the low country, and of the south of Yehuda, and had taken Beth-shemesh, and Ayalon, and Gederoth, and Shocho with the villages thereof, and Timnah with the villages thereof, Gimzo also and the villages thereof: and they dwelt there.
For the YAHAWAH brought Yehuda low because of Ahaz king of YisraEL; for he made Yehuda naked, and transgressed sore against the YAHAWAH.
And Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria came unto him, and distressed him, but strengthened him not.
For Ahaz took away a portion out of the house of the YAHAWAH, and out of the house of the king, and of the princes, and gave it unto the king of Assyria: but he helped him not.
¶ And in the time of his distress did he trespass yet more against the YAHAWAH: this is that King Ahaz.

For he sacrificed unto the elohiyms of Damascus, which smote him: and he said, Because the elohiyms of the kings of Syria help them, therefore will I sacrifice to them, that they may help me. But they were the ruin of him, and of all YisraEL.

And Ahaz gathered together the vessels of the house of ELOHIYM, and cut in pieces the vessels of the house of ELOHIYM, and shut up the doors of the house of the YAHAWAH, and he made him altars in every corner of Yerushalayim.
And in every several city of Yehuda he made high places to burn incense unto other elohiyms, and provoked to anger the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of his fathers.
¶ Now the rest of his acts and of all his ways, first and last, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Yehuda and YisraEL.

And Ahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, even in Yerushalayim: but they brought him not into the sepulchres of the kings of YisraEL: and HezekYah his son reigned in his stead.
HezekYah began to reign when he was five and twenty years old, and he reigned nine and twenty years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was AbiYah, the daughter of ZecharYah.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the YAHAWAH, according to all that David his father had done.
¶ He in the first year of his reign, in the first month, opened the doors of the house of the YAHAWAH, and repaired them.
And he brought in the priests and the Levites, and gathered them together into the east street,
And said unto them, Hear me, ye Levites, sanctify now yourselves, and sanctify the house of the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of your fathers, and carry forth the filthiness out of the holy place.

For our fathers have trespassed, and done that which was evil in the eyes of the YAHAWAH our ELOHIYM, and have forsaken him, and have turned away their faces from the habitation of the YAHAWAH, and turned their backs.
Also they have shut up the doors of the porch, and put out the lamps, and have not burned incense nor offered burnt offerings in the holy place unto the ELOHIYM of YisraEL.
Wherefore the wrath of the YAHAWAH was upon Yehuda and Yerushalayim, and he hath delivered them to trouble, to astonishment, and to hissing, as ye see with your eyes.
For, lo, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives are in captivity for this.
Now it is in mine heart to make a covenant with the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of YisraEL, that his fierce wrath may turn away from us.
My sons, be not now negligent: for the YAHAWAH hath chosen you to stand before him, to serve him, and that ye should minister unto him, and burn incense.

¶ Then the Levites arose, Mahath the son of Amasai, and Yo’el the son of AzarYah, of the sons of the Kohathites: and of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi, and AzarYah the son of Yehalel’el: and of the Gershonites; Yo’ach the son of Zimmah, and Eden the son of Yo’ach:
And of the sons of Elizaphan; Shimri, and Yei’el: and of the sons of Asaph; ZecharYah, and MattanYah:
And of the sons of Heman; Yei’el, and Shimei: and of the sons of Yedutun; ShemaYah, and Uzziel.
And they gathered their brethren, and sanctified themselves, and came, according to the commandment of the king, by the words of the YAHAWAH, to cleanse the house of the YAHAWAH.

And the priests went into the inner part of the house of the YAHAWAH, to cleanse it, and brought out all the uncleanness that they found in the temple of the YAHAWAH into the court of the house of the YAHAWAH. And the Levites took it, to carry it out abroad into the brook Kidron.

Now they began on the first day of the first month to sanctify, and on the eighth day of the month came they to the porch of the YAHAWAH: so they sanctified the house of the YAHAWAH in eight days; and in the sixteenth day of the first month they made an end.

Then they went in to HezekYah the king, and said, We have cleansed all the house of the YAHAWAH, and the altar of burnt offering, with all the vessels thereof, and the shewbread table, with all the vessels thereof.
Moreover all the vessels, which king Ahaz in his reign did cast away in his transgression, have we prepared and sanctified, and, behold, they are before the altar of the YAHAWAH.
¶ Then HezekYah the king rose early, and gathered the rulers of the city, and went up to the house of the YAHAWAH.

And they brought seven bullocks, and seven rams, and seven lambs, and seven he goats, for a sin offering for the kingdom, and for the sanctuary, and for Yehuda. And he commanded the priests the sons of Aaron to offer them on the altar of the YAHAWAH.

So they killed the bullocks, and the priests received the blood, and sprinkled it on the altar: likewise, when they had killed the rams, they sprinkled the blood upon the altar: they killed also the lambs, and they sprinkled the blood upon the altar.
And they brought forth the he goats for the sin offering before the king and the congregation; and they laid their hands upon them:

And the priests killed them, and they made reconciliation with their blood upon the altar, to make an atonement for all YisraEL: for the king commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering should be made for all YisraEL.

And he set the Levites in the house of the YAHAWAH with cymbals, with psalteries, and with harps, according to the commandment of David, and of Gad the king’s seer, and Nathan the prophet: for so was the commandment of the YAHAWAH by his prophets.
And the Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.

And HezekYah commanded to offer the burnt offering upon the altar. And when the burnt offering began, the song of the YAHAWAH began also with the trumpets, and with the instruments ordained by David king of YisraEL.
And all the congregation worshipped, and the singers sang, and the trumTzuri’els sounded: and all this continued until the burnt offering was finished.
And when they had made an end of offering, the king and all that were present with him bowed themselves, and worshipped.

Moreover HezekYah the king and the princes commanded the Levites to sing praise unto the YAHAWAH with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer. And they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshipped.

Then HezekYah answered and said, Now ye have consecrated yourselves unto the YAHAWAH, come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings into the house of the YAHAWAH. And the congregation brought in sacrifices and thank offerings; and as many as were of a free heart burnt offerings.
And the number of the burnt offerings, which the congregation brought, was threescore and ten bullocks, an hundred rams, and two hundred lambs: all these were for a burnt offering to the YAHAWAH.
And the consecrated things were six hundred oxen and three thousand sheep.

But the priests were too few, so that they could not flay all the burnt offerings: wherefore their brethren the Levites did help them, till the work was ended, and until the other priests had sanctified themselves: for the Levites were more upright in heart to sanctify themselves than the priests.
And also the burnt offerings were in abundance, with the fat of the peace offerings, and the drink offerings for every burnt offering. So the service of the house of the YAHAWAH was set in order.
And HezekYah praised, and all the people, that ELOHIYM had prepared the people: for the thing was done suddenly.

And HezekYah sent to all YisraEL and Yehuda, and wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the house of the YAHAWAH at Yerushalayim, to keep the Passover unto the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of YisraEL.
For the king had taken counsel, and his princes, and all the congregation in Yerushalayim, to keep the Passover in the second month.
For they could not keep it at that time, because the priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently, neither had the people gathered themselves together to Yerushalayim.
And the thing pleased the king and all the congregation.

So they established a decree to make proclamation throughout all YisraEL, from Beer-sheba even to Dan, that they should come to keep the Passover unto the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of YisraEL at Yerushalayim: for they had not done it of a long time in such sort as it was written.

So the posts went with the letters from the king and his princes throughout all YisraEL and Yehuda, and according to the commandment of the king, saying, Ye children of YisraEL, turn again unto the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of Abraham, Isaac, and YisraEL, and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria.
And be not ye like your fathers, and like your brethren, which trespassed against the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of their fathers, who therefore gave them up to desolation, as ye see.

Now be ye not stiffnecked, as your fathers were, but yield yourselves unto the YAHAWAH, and enter into his sanctuary, which he hath sanctified for ever: and serve the YAHAWAH your ELOHIYM, that the fierceness of his wrath may turn away from you.

For if ye turn again unto the YAHAWAH, your brethren and your children shall find compassion before them that lead them captive, so that they shall come again into this land: for the YAHAWAH your ELOHIYM is gracious and merciful, and will not turn away his face from you, if ye return unto him.
So the posts passed from city to city through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh even unto Zebulun: but they laughed them to scorn, and mocked them.
Nevertheless divers of Asher and Manasseh and of Zebulun humbled themselves, and came to Yerushalayim.
Also in Yehuda the hand of ELOHIYM was to give them one heart to do the commandment of the king and of the princes, by the word of the YAHAWAH.
¶ And there assembled at Yerushalayim much people to keep the feast of unleavened bread in the second month, a very great congregation.
And they arose and took away the altars that were in Yerushalayim, and all the altars for incense took they away, and cast them into the brook Kidron.

Then they killed the passover on the fourteenth day of the second month: and the priests and the Levites were ashamed, and sanctified themselves, and brought in the burnt offerings into the house of the YAHAWAH.
And they stood in their place after their manner, according to the Law of Moses the man of ELOHIYM: the priests sprinkled the blood, which they received of the hand of the Levites.

For there were many in the congregation that were not sanctified: therefore the Levites had the charge of the killing of the Passovers for every one that was not clean, to sanctify them unto the YAHAWAH.

For a multitude of the people, even many of Ephraim, and Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves, yet did they eat the Passover otherwise than it was written. But HezekYah prayed for them, saying, The good YAHAWAH pardon every one
That prepareth his heart to seek ELOHIYM, the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of his fathers, though he be not cleansed according to the purification of the sanctuary.
And the YAHAWAH hearkened to HezekYah, and healed the people.

And the children of YisraEL that were present at Yerushalayim kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness: and the Levites and the priests praised the YAHAWAH day by day, singing with loud instruments unto the YAHAWAH.

And HezekYah spake comfortably unto all the Levites that taught the good knowledge of the YAHAWAH: and they did eat throughout the feast seven days, offering peace offerings, and making confession to the YAHAWAH ELOHIYM of their fathers.
